UBS raised its price target on Micron $MU to $1,625 from $535 while maintaining a Buy rating, citing structural changes in the memory market driven by AI. The firm expects Micron’s EPS to stay above $100 through 2029 and sees the company generating more than $400B in free cash flow over that period. UBS also pointed to long-term agreements across the memory industry that could lock in pricing and create a smoother earnings profile. Micron has now passed $1 trillion in market cap, making it the 9th largest company in the world.

*Samsung Electronics Union Says Members Approve Wage Deal



Under the agreement, chip workers receive a cash bonus equal to 50% of annual salary plus stock bonuses tied to 10.5% of chip‑division operating profit; some memory workers may net up to ~$416,000 in total bonuses



The tentative deal came amid worker unrest over pay gaps—especially compared to rival SK Hynix—and escalated after union pressure and government intervention; approval now defuses the most serious labor crisis at Samsung in years
